patient_explanation: The heart appears larger than normal on the scan.
clinical_context: Seen on chest X-rays. May indicate heart strain, cardiomyopathy, or fluid around the heart.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There is extra fluid in the space around the lungs.
clinical_context: Can result from heart failure, infection, malignancy, or inflammation. May cause breathlessness.
action_note: A doctor can explain the cause and next steps.
follow_up: Thoracentesis may be needed for diagnosis or treatment

simple_meaning: Part of the lung is not fully open
patient_explanation: A small part of the lung is partly collapsed or not fully expanded.
clinical_context: Common post-operatively or due to mucus plugging. Usually temporary and reversible.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Breathing exercises or physiotherapy often recommended

patient_explanation: A bone is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Seen on X-rays after injury. Can be cortical, hairline, comminuted, or pathological.
action_note: Medical review is needed to decide treatment.

simple_meaning: Area of lung filled with infection or fluid
patient_explanation: Part of the lung appears denser than normal, often due to infection or inflammation.
clinical_context: Often seen with pneumonia. Air is replaced by fluid, pus, or cells.
action_note: A healthcare professional can explain the cause and treatment if needed.
follow_up: Antibiotics if infective; repeat imaging may confirm resolution

patient_explanation: Air is trapped around the lung, which can cause part of the lung to collapse.
clinical_context: Can be spontaneous or traumatic. Tension pneumothorax is a medical emergency.
action_note: This should be reviewed urgently by a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Urgent chest drain if large; observation if small

patient_explanation: There is scarring in part of the tissue seen on the scan.
clinical_context: Result of chronic inflammation. Can reduce lung flexibility.
action_note: A doctor can explain whether follow-up is needed.
follow_up: Pulmonologist review; PFTs and HRCT may be considered

patient_explanation: Bleeding has been detected in the scanned area.
clinical_context: In brain imaging this may include subdural, epidural, subarachnoid, or intracerebral bleeding.
action_note: Urgent medical review may be needed.
follow_up: Neurosurgery review; blood pressure control may be needed

patient_explanation: Extra fluid is causing swelling in the tissue.
clinical_context: Can occur in many areas. Significance depends on location and cause.
action_note: The cause should be discussed with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: An area looks different from normal tissue. It does not always mean cancer.
clinical_context: Broad term covering any focal abnormality. Nature depends on size, location, and imaging features.
action_note: Further evaluation may be recommended.
follow_up: MRI with contrast or biopsy may be needed

patient_explanation: A small spot was seen on the scan.
clinical_context: Lung nodules are commonly monitored depending on size and appearance.
action_note: A doctor may recommend monitoring or additional imaging.
follow_up: Follow-up CT may be recommended depending on guidelines

patient_explanation: There is calcium build-up in the tissue or blood vessel.
clinical_context: Can occur with aging, previous inflammation, or vascular disease.
action_note: This is often a chronic or older finding.
follow_up: Usually no action required unless clinically significant

patient_explanation: The scan shows changes that commonly happen over time with aging or joint use.
clinical_context: Includes osteophytes, disc space narrowing, and subchondral sclerosis. Very common with age.
action_note: A doctor can explain if treatment or exercises may help.
follow_up: Physiotherapy; pain management; orthopaedic review if severe

patient_explanation: The scanned area looks normal and no significant problem was seen.
clinical_context: Standard radiology term for normal findings.
action_note: This is generally reassuring.

patient_explanation: A larger abnormal lump or growth was seen on the scan.
clinical_context: Can be benign or malignant and often needs further characterization.
action_note: This should be discussed with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Biopsy or further imaging often required

patient_explanation: Part of the lung shows changes that may be due to infection, fluid, or inflammation.
clinical_context: Non-specific term. Often requires clinical correlation.
action_note: A doctor can explain whether treatment or follow-up is needed.
follow_up: Cultures; antibiotics if infective; repeat imaging

patient_explanation: The lungs appear more inflated than usual on the scan.
clinical_context: Indicates air trapping and may be associated with COPD or asthma.
action_note: This should be interpreted with breathing symptoms and medical history.
follow_up: Pulmonary function tests; respiratory physician review

patient_explanation: The lining around the lungs appears thicker than usual.
clinical_context: Can occur after infection, inflammation, exposure, or injury.
action_note: A healthcare professional can explain if follow-up is required.
follow_up: Occupational history important; CT may be needed

simple_meaning: Damage to air spaces in the lungs
patient_explanation: The scan shows changes in the lungs that can make breathing less efficient.
clinical_context: Permanent air-space damage. Often related to smoking or chronic lung irritation.
action_note: Discuss this with a healthcare professional, especially if there are breathing symptoms.

patient_explanation: There is extra fluid in the lung tissue.
clinical_context: Can be related to heart failure, kidney problems, or fluid overload.
action_note: This should be reviewed promptly by a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Urgent assessment; oxygen/diuretics may be needed

patient_explanation: Some brain structures appear pushed away from their usual position.
clinical_context: Can happen when swelling, bleeding, or pressure pushes brain structures.
action_note: This usually needs urgent medical review.
follow_up: Neurosurgical emergency; ICP monitoring may be needed

patient_explanation: An area may not be getting enough blood supply.
clinical_context: In brain imaging, this can relate to stroke-like changes.
action_note: This should be reviewed by a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Stroke team assessment may be needed

simple_meaning: Tissue damage from reduced blood supply
patient_explanation: An area of tissue may have been damaged because of reduced blood flow.
clinical_context: In brain reports, this often refers to stroke-related damage.
action_note: A doctor can explain whether it is new or old and what it means.
follow_up: Neurology review; antiplatelet or anticoagulation depending on cause

simple_meaning: Shrinkage or loss of tissue volume
patient_explanation: Some tissue appears smaller than expected.
clinical_context: In brain imaging, mild atrophy can be age-related.
action_note: A doctor can explain if this is expected for age or needs follow-up.

patient_explanation: Small bony outgrowths have formed at the edges of a joint.
clinical_context: A response to cartilage loss or wear-and-tear. Common with age.
action_note: Usually age-related; physiotherapy or pain management may help.

patient_explanation: One of the cushioning discs between spinal bones has bulged out of place.
clinical_context: Most common in lower spine. Can press on nerves and cause sciatica-like symptoms.
action_note: Neurosurgical or orthopaedic review may be needed depending on symptoms.
follow_up: Physiotherapy; pain management; surgery if neurological deficit

patient_explanation: Too much cerebrospinal fluid has built up inside the brain cavities.
clinical_context: Can increase pressure in the brain and may need urgent assessment.
action_note: This usually requires urgent neurosurgical assessment.
follow_up: Neurosurgical review; shunt may be needed

patient_explanation: An area of bone appears to be breaking down or being eaten away.
clinical_context: Can be aggressive and requires further assessment to find the cause.
action_note: This needs urgent follow-up with a specialist.
follow_up: Oncology; bone biopsy; whole body staging

patient_explanation: Part of the lung looks hazy, like frosted glass, while structures underneath may still be seen.
clinical_context: Often reflects infection, inflammation, edema, or scarring depending on context.
action_note: Follow-up imaging or clinical correlation may be needed.
follow_up: Repeat CT in 3-6 months if persistent; PFTs

patient_explanation: The lymph nodes appear larger than normal.
clinical_context: Can occur with infection, inflammation, immune conditions, or cancer.
action_note: The cause needs to be determined with further tests.
follow_up: Blood tests; biopsy if persistent or large

patient_explanation: The liver appears larger than expected on the scan.
clinical_context: Can be associated with fatty liver, hepatitis, heart failure, or infiltration.
action_note: Liver function tests and further imaging are usually advised.

patient_explanation: The spleen appears larger than normal on the scan.
clinical_context: Can be linked with infection, liver disease, or blood conditions.
action_note: Blood tests and cause evaluation may be needed.

patient_explanation: Stones have been found inside the gallbladder.
clinical_context: Often incidental unless causing pain or inflammation.
action_note: If asymptomatic, may not need treatment. See a doctor if you have pain.

patient_explanation: A stone has been found in the kidney or urinary tract.
clinical_context: Most small stones pass naturally. Obstruction changes urgency.
action_note: Pain management and urology review if large.
follow_up: Urology review if >5mm or obstructing; hydration

simple_meaning: Swelling of the kidney due to blocked urine flow
patient_explanation: Urine is not draining properly from the kidney, causing it to swell.
clinical_context: Can happen due to stone, stricture, tumour, enlarged prostate, or pregnancy.
action_note: Urology review is needed especially if bilateral or worsening.
follow_up: Urology; nephrostomy if severe; treat underlying cause

patient_explanation: The main blood vessel in the body has ballooned or bulged in one area.
clinical_context: Size and symptoms determine urgency. Large aneurysms may need repair.
action_note: Urgent vascular surgery review if large or symptomatic.
follow_up: Vascular surgery review; surveillance or repair depending on size

patient_explanation: A blood clot has blocked one of the arteries supplying the lungs.
clinical_context: CTPA is commonly used. Requires urgent medical treatment.
action_note: This requires urgent medical treatment with blood thinners.

simple_meaning: Blood clot in a deep vein
patient_explanation: A blood clot has formed in one of the deep veins, usually in the leg.
clinical_context: Doppler ultrasound is diagnostic. Untreated clots can travel to the lungs.
action_note: Requires urgent blood thinners to prevent clot spreading to lungs.

simple_meaning: Narrowing of a blood vessel or passage
patient_explanation: A blood vessel or opening has become narrower than normal, reducing flow through it.
clinical_context: Significance depends on location and degree of narrowing.
action_note: The degree of narrowing determines urgency; discuss with your doctor.
follow_up: Angioplasty, stenting, or surgery depending on site and severity

simple_meaning: Area that lights up with contrast dye
patient_explanation: After contrast dye was injected, this area appeared brighter.
clinical_context: Enhancement helps doctors assess blood supply or abnormal tissue behavior.
action_note: Enhancement pattern helps characterise the abnormality.
follow_up: Biopsy or specialist review depending on location

patient_explanation: Too much fat has accumulated in the liver tissue.
clinical_context: Common finding that can improve with lifestyle change.
action_note: Lifestyle changes such as diet and exercise are important.
follow_up: LFTs; hepatology if advanced; weight loss programme

patient_explanation: Free fluid has collected inside the abdomen.
clinical_context: Can be due to liver disease, heart failure, cancer, or infection.
action_note: The cause needs to be investigated.

patient_explanation: The tube that drains the pancreas appears wider than normal.
clinical_context: Can happen with obstruction, chronic pancreatitis, cystic lesions, stones, or tumour.
action_note: Specialist review needed to exclude serious causes.
follow_up: MRCP; gastroenterology; oncology if malignancy suspected

simple_meaning: Free air in the abdomen — possible organ perforation
patient_explanation: Air has been found in an area where it should not normally be.
clinical_context: Can suggest pneumoperitoneum and possible bowel or stomach perforation.
action_note: This is a surgical emergency; urgent review needed.
follow_up: Urgent surgical review; laparotomy may be required

patient_explanation: The outer working layer of the kidney appears thinner than normal.
clinical_context: Can indicate chronic kidney disease or long-standing obstruction.
action_note: Kidney function blood tests are needed.

patient_explanation: One of the spinal bones has slipped forward over the bone below it.
clinical_context: Can cause back pain or nerve symptoms depending on severity.
action_note: Physiotherapy and pain management are usually first-line.

patient_explanation: An area of tissue or bone has become harder or denser than normal.
clinical_context: In joints this is often from arthritis; elsewhere significance depends on context.
action_note: Context determines significance; discuss with your doctor.
follow_up: Depends on context; often incidental in osteoarthritis

patient_explanation: A small sac filled with fluid was seen on the scan. These are usually harmless.
clinical_context: Simple cysts are usually benign. Complex cysts may need follow-up.
action_note: Simple cysts are almost always benign. Complex ones need review.
follow_up: Surveillance if complex; no action for simple benign cysts

simple_meaning: Cloudiness around the centre of the lungs
patient_explanation: The area around the centre of the lungs appears hazy or cloudy on the X-ray.
clinical_context: Can be seen with pulmonary edema, pulmonary hypertension, or infection.
action_note: Usually associated with heart or lung conditions; discuss with your doctor.
follow_up: Cardiology review; echocardiogram may be needed

patient_explanation: The intestine appears blocked, preventing normal passage of contents.
clinical_context: Can cause abdominal pain, vomiting, swelling, and inability to pass gas/stool.
action_note: This requires urgent surgical evaluation.
follow_up: Surgical review; NG tube; IV fluids; possible surgery

patient_explanation: There is extra fluid in the sac surrounding the heart.
clinical_context: Can be caused by infection, inflammation, cancer, or kidney failure; large amounts can affect heart function.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: Fluid buildup around the heart is pressing on it, which can stop it working properly.
clinical_context: A medical emergency where pericardial fluid raises pressure enough to impair heart filling.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The heart muscle isn't working or shaped the way it normally should.
clinical_context: Umbrella term covering dilated, hypertrophic, or restrictive patterns affecting heart pump function.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Thickened wall of the heart's main pumping chamber
patient_explanation: The main pumping chamber of the heart has thicker walls than normal.
clinical_context: Commonly related to longstanding high blood pressure or valve disease increasing heart workload.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Blood pressure control and cardiology review

patient_explanation: One of the heart's valves isn't closing fully, so some blood leaks backward.
clinical_context: Graded mild to severe; severe leakage can lead to heart enlargement or failure over time.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The valve that lets blood leave the heart's main chamber has become narrowed.
clinical_context: Restricts blood flow out of the heart; severe cases can cause chest pain, fainting, or breathlessness.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Cardiology follow-up; may need valve replacement if severe

patient_explanation: Small deposits of calcium have built up in the arteries that supply the heart.
clinical_context: A marker of underlying atherosclerosis (artery hardening); often quantified with a calcium score.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Discuss cardiovascular risk factors with your doctor

patient_explanation: One of the smaller, upper chambers of the heart appears larger than usual.
clinical_context: Often reflects longstanding high pressure or valve disease affecting that chamber.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Right heart strain from lung disease
patient_explanation: The right side of the heart is under strain, usually because of a lung problem.
clinical_context: Right ventricular enlargement/dysfunction secondary to chronic lung disease or pulmonary hypertension.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Wire from a heart device seen on imaging
patient_explanation: A thin wire from a heart pacemaker or defibrillator is visible on the scan; this is expected if you have one.
clinical_context: Not itself a finding of concern; position is usually checked for correct placement.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Routine device check with cardiology as scheduled

patient_explanation: One of the heart's valves on the right side isn't closing fully, letting some blood flow backward.
clinical_context: Often mild and incidental, but can indicate right heart strain when moderate-severe.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Calcium buildup on the aortic valve
patient_explanation: The valve that controls blood leaving the heart has calcium deposits on it.
clinical_context: Can progress to aortic stenosis over time; often age-related.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Hole between the heart's lower chambers
patient_explanation: There is a small opening in the wall separating the two main pumping chambers of the heart.
clinical_context: May be congenital (present from birth) or, rarely, acquired after a heart attack; size determines significance.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Heart appears large relative to chest
patient_explanation: The heart's size compared to the chest cavity is larger than the usual range.
clinical_context: A simple screening sign on chest X-ray that can suggest cardiomegaly or fluid overload.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

patient_explanation: There is evidence of old, healed damage to part of the heart muscle.
clinical_context: Typically reflects a prior heart attack or inflammatory event; can affect pump function.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The valve controlling blood leaving the heart's main chamber isn't sealing fully, letting blood leak backward.
clinical_context: Can cause the heart's main chamber to enlarge over time if moderate-severe.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: Metal wires used to close the breastbone after previous heart surgery are visible; this is expected.
clinical_context: Not a new finding of concern; confirms history of prior sternotomy (open-heart surgery).
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: No specific follow-up needed for the wires themselves

patient_explanation: The right pumping chamber of the heart appears larger than normal.
clinical_context: Often related to lung disease, pulmonary hypertension, or valve problems raising pressure on that side.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The heart isn't pumping out as much blood with each beat as it normally would.
clinical_context: A key measure of heart failure severity, usually obtained on echocardiogram.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Cardiology follow-up for heart failure management

simple_meaning: Widened base of the main artery
patient_explanation: The section of the main artery closest to the heart is wider than the usual range.
clinical_context: Monitored over time as significant enlargement raises risk of aortic dissection or rupture.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The tubes that carry air into the lungs are permanently widened and scarred.
clinical_context: Leads to mucus buildup and recurrent infections; can be localized or widespread.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There are changes in the fine lung tissue that can make breathing less efficient over time.
clinical_context: Umbrella term for many conditions causing lung scarring or inflammation of the interstitium.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There's a small area of thickening on the lining that covers the lungs.
clinical_context: Frequently related to past asbestos exposure; usually benign but noted for monitoring.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Routine monitoring, no urgent action typically needed

patient_explanation: There is an infection in part of the lung tissue.
clinical_context: Common cause of consolidation on imaging; severity ranges from mild to life-threatening.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Antibiotics and follow-up imaging as advised

simple_meaning: Small branching pattern in the lungs
patient_explanation: A pattern that looks like tiny budding branches shows up on the scan, often linked to small airway inflammation.
clinical_context: Classically associated with infections that affect the small airways, including tuberculosis.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Further work-up guided by clinical symptoms

simple_meaning: Cluster of small air-filled cysts in scarred lung
patient_explanation: Part of the lung tissue has a pattern of small cyst-like spaces, usually a sign of advanced scarring.
clinical_context: A hallmark feature of advanced pulmonary fibrosis, particularly usual interstitial pneumonia pattern.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Hollow space within a lung abnormality
patient_explanation: There's an abnormal area in the lung that has a hollow, air-filled centre.
clinical_context: Can occur with infection (including tuberculosis), abscess, or certain tumours.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Prompt clinical correlation and further work-up advised

simple_meaning: Large air-filled sac in the lung
patient_explanation: There is a large air-filled pocket within the lung tissue, often from damaged, stretched lung.
clinical_context: Common in emphysema; large bullae can occasionally rupture causing pneumothorax.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Air in the chest cavity around the heart
patient_explanation: There is air present in the central chest space around the heart and major vessels, which isn't normally there.
clinical_context: Can result from airway or oesophageal injury, or spontaneously from a ruptured air sac.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Widespread tiny nodules in the lungs
patient_explanation: Many very small spots are scattered evenly throughout both lungs.
clinical_context: Classic pattern associated with disseminated infection (e.g. tuberculosis) spreading through the bloodstream.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Net-like marking pattern in the lungs
patient_explanation: A fine, web-like pattern of lines is visible across part of the lung tissue.
clinical_context: Often an early or associated feature of interstitial lung disease.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Visible airways within a lung abnormality
patient_explanation: The small air tubes inside the lungs are visible within an area of abnormal lung tissue, which happens when the tissue around them fills with fluid or infection.
clinical_context: A useful sign that helps confirm consolidation (fluid/infection-filled lung) rather than other causes.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Correlate with clinical symptoms and treatment response

simple_meaning: Short horizontal lines at lung edges
patient_explanation: Small horizontal lines appear near the outer edges of the lungs, a sign linked to fluid buildup.
clinical_context: Represents fluid in the tiny lymphatic channels of the lung, classically from heart failure.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: Air trapped outside the lung is building up pressure and pushing on the heart and the other lung.
clinical_context: A life-threatening emergency requiring immediate needle or chest tube decompression.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Air and fluid together outside the lung
patient_explanation: There is both air and fluid trapped in the space around the lung.
clinical_context: Can follow trauma, surgery, or infection with a fluid collection that has also released gas.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: Thick mucus is blocking part of an airway, which can cause the section of lung it supplies to collapse slightly.
clinical_context: Common cause of atelectasis, especially post-operatively or in chronic airway disease.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Breathing exercises or physiotherapy often recommended

simple_meaning: Lung lining stuck to chest wall
patient_explanation: Part of the lining around the lung has become stuck to the chest wall, usually from previous inflammation.
clinical_context: Typically a sign of prior pleural inflammation, infection, or surgery; usually not itself concerning.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Old healed scarring at the top of the lung
patient_explanation: There's old scar tissue at the very top of one or both lungs, usually from a past infection.
clinical_context: Commonly a residual finding from prior tuberculosis or other old infection; usually stable.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Compare with prior imaging if available

simple_meaning: Small spot near the lung surface
patient_explanation: A small spot has been found just beneath the outer surface of the lung.
clinical_context: Location and size guide whether follow-up imaging or biopsy is recommended.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Follow-up CT often recommended depending on size

patient_explanation: The central area of the chest between the lungs looks wider than expected.
clinical_context: Can be due to benign fat, lymph node enlargement, or more serious causes like aortic injury.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The area where the major airways and vessels enter the lung looks larger than usual.
clinical_context: Can reflect enlarged lymph nodes, prominent vessels, or, less often, a mass.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Further imaging may be advised if new or enlarging

simple_meaning: High blood pressure in the lung arteries
patient_explanation: The blood pressure in the arteries supplying the lungs is higher than normal.
clinical_context: Increases strain on the right side of the heart; can be primary or secondary to lung/heart disease.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The walls of the breathing tubes in the lungs appear thicker than usual.
clinical_context: A nonspecific finding often related to inflammation, infection, or chronic airway disease.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Small blood clot in a lung artery branch
patient_explanation: A small blood clot is blocking one of the smaller branches of a lung artery.
clinical_context: Smaller than a main pulmonary embolism but still requires clinical assessment for treatment.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: Part of the lung tissue has lost its normal elastic structure and become over-inflated.
clinical_context: Reflects breakdown of lung air sacs, most often from smoking.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Rounded edge at the base of the lung
patient_explanation: The normally sharp angle at the bottom edge of the lung looks rounded rather than pointed.
clinical_context: A subtle early sign that can indicate a small amount of fluid around the lung.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Correlate clinically; further imaging if symptomatic

patient_explanation: The cushioning cartilage in a joint has worn down, which is a common part of joint ageing.
clinical_context: The most common form of arthritis, causing joint space narrowing, osteophytes, and stiffness.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Physiotherapy and pain management as advised

patient_explanation: The bones have become thinner and more fragile than normal, raising the risk of fractures.
clinical_context: A systemic condition reducing bone density, often assessed with a DEXA scan.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: DEXA scan and bone health review recommended

patient_explanation: Bone density is a little lower than normal, though not as low as osteoporosis.
clinical_context: Considered an early stage of bone density loss; monitored to prevent progression.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Bone health review with your doctor recommended

patient_explanation: One of the bones in the spine has partially collapsed, often becoming shorter or wedge-shaped.
clinical_context: Common in osteoporosis but can also follow trauma; may cause back pain and height loss.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Spine specialist or orthopaedic follow-up recommended

patient_explanation: A tiny crack has formed in a bone due to repeated stress, rather than a single injury.
clinical_context: Common in weight-bearing bones with repetitive activity, such as running.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Rest and activity modification typically advised

simple_meaning: Small bone fragment pulled off by a tendon/ligament
patient_explanation: A small piece of bone has been pulled away from the main bone by a tendon or ligament.
clinical_context: Occurs where a tendon or ligament attaches, often from sudden forceful contraction.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Joint bones out of normal position
patient_explanation: The bones that form a joint have moved out of their normal alignment.
clinical_context: Requires prompt reduction (repositioning) to restore normal joint alignment and function.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The bones of a joint are partly out of position, but not fully dislocated.
clinical_context: A milder form of joint displacement, still needing assessment to prevent recurrence or instability.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

patient_explanation: The cartilage cushion inside the knee that absorbs shock has a tear.
clinical_context: Common knee injury from twisting movements or degeneration; severity varies widely.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: One of the main ligaments that stabilises the knee is torn.
clinical_context: A common sports injury that can cause knee instability; may need surgical reconstruction.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: One or more of the tendons that help move and stabilise the shoulder is torn.
clinical_context: Common with age-related degeneration or after a fall/injury; severity ranges from partial to full-thickness.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: The ring of cartilage that deepens a joint socket (shoulder or hip) has a tear.
clinical_context: Can cause pain, clicking, or instability in the affected joint.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

patient_explanation: There is extra fluid within the bone itself, usually a sign of stress or minor injury.
clinical_context: A sensitive but nonspecific MRI finding suggesting bone stress, bruising, or early fracture.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Rest and follow-up imaging if symptoms persist

simple_meaning: New bone forming on the bone surface
patient_explanation: The lining of the bone is producing new bone tissue in response to irritation, injury, or infection.
clinical_context: Pattern of periosteal reaction can help distinguish benign from more concerning causes.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Further evaluation recommended to determine cause

patient_explanation: There is more fluid than usual inside a joint space.
clinical_context: A nonspecific sign of joint irritation that can accompany injury, arthritis, or infection.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Correlate with symptoms; further work-up if infection suspected

patient_explanation: The lining tissue inside a joint is inflamed.
clinical_context: Can accompany arthritis, injury, or infection; often causes swelling and pain.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Rheumatology or orthopaedic follow-up as advised

patient_explanation: A tendon shows signs of long-term wear and thickening rather than a fresh injury.
clinical_context: Represents chronic degenerative change from repetitive stress, distinct from acute tendon inflammation.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Inflamed cushioning sac near a joint
patient_explanation: A small fluid-filled sac that cushions a joint is inflamed and swollen.
clinical_context: Common around the shoulder, hip, elbow, or knee, often from repetitive friction or pressure.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Rest and anti-inflammatory measures typically advised

patient_explanation: The cartilage on the underside of the kneecap has softened and is wearing down.
clinical_context: A common cause of anterior knee pain, particularly in younger, active people.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

patient_explanation: The spine curves to one side more than the normal, straight alignment.
clinical_context: Can be mild and incidental or more significant, sometimes needing monitoring or bracing.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Spine specialist follow-up if curve is significant

simple_meaning: Excessive forward curve of the upper spine
patient_explanation: The upper back curves forward more than normal, sometimes giving a rounded or hunched appearance.
clinical_context: Can be postural, age-related, or due to compression fractures affecting the spine.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

patient_explanation: The spine shows general wear-and-tear changes that are common with age.
clinical_context: An umbrella term for age-related degenerative changes affecting discs and joints of the spine.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Physiotherapy and pain management as advised

patient_explanation: The small joints at the back of the spine that guide movement show wear-and-tear changes.
clinical_context: A common source of back pain related to degenerative changes in the small spinal joints.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Physiotherapy and pain management as advised

patient_explanation: The channel in the spine that houses the spinal cord or nerves has become narrower than normal.
clinical_context: Can compress nerves, causing pain, numbness, or weakness, particularly with standing or walking.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Inflammation of the lower back/pelvis joint
patient_explanation: The joint connecting the base of the spine to the pelvis is inflamed.
clinical_context: Can be linked to inflammatory arthritis conditions or mechanical strain.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Rheumatology follow-up if inflammatory cause suspected

patient_explanation: There is an infection within the bone itself.
clinical_context: A serious infection requiring prompt antibiotic treatment, and sometimes surgery, to prevent bone damage.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There is a fluid-filled space within the bone, which is usually a benign, non-cancerous finding.
clinical_context: Most bone cysts are benign and found incidentally; monitored to ensure stability over time.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Follow-up imaging if size or symptoms change

patient_explanation: There is a small, usually harmless growth of cartilage tissue inside a bone.
clinical_context: One of the most common benign bone tumours, often found incidentally on imaging.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Bone tissue dying from lost blood supply
patient_explanation: Part of a bone has lost its blood supply, causing the bone tissue in that area to die.
clinical_context: Can lead to bone collapse over time if untreated; the hip is a commonly affected site.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Tiny old bleeds in the brain
patient_explanation: Very small, old areas of bleeding are scattered within the brain tissue.
clinical_context: Often related to small blood vessel disease and are a marker of bleeding risk on certain scans.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Bright spots in the brain's white matter
patient_explanation: Small bright areas are seen in the deeper white matter of the brain on certain scan sequences.
clinical_context: A common, often age-related finding linked to small blood vessel changes; significance depends on extent.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Correlate with clinical symptoms and vascular risk factors

patient_explanation: There are diffuse changes in the deep brain tissue that are commonly seen with ageing and small blood vessel changes.
clinical_context: A descriptive term for chronic small vessel ischemic changes in the brain's white matter.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Bleeding between the brain and its outer covering
patient_explanation: There is a collection of blood between the brain surface and its outer protective layer.
clinical_context: Can follow head trauma, especially in older adults; may require urgent surgical drainage if large.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Bleeding between the skull and brain covering
patient_explanation: There is a collection of blood between the inner skull surface and the brain's outer covering.
clinical_context: A neurosurgical emergency, often following skull fracture, that can rapidly raise brain pressure.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There is bleeding into the space surrounding the brain, between the brain and its covering membranes.
clinical_context: A medical emergency, often from a ruptured aneurysm, presenting classically with sudden severe headache.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Bleeding into the brain's fluid chambers
patient_explanation: There is bleeding into the fluid-filled chambers deep inside the brain.
clinical_context: Can occur alongside other types of brain bleeding and may obstruct normal fluid drainage.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There is swelling within the brain tissue.
clinical_context: Can raise pressure inside the skull and is often associated with injury, stroke, or tumour.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Brain structures pushed out of position
patient_explanation: An abnormal area is large enough to be pushing on and displacing the normal brain structures nearby.
clinical_context: An important sign that guides urgency, as significant mass effect can raise pressure inside the skull.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Brain tissue pushed out of its normal space
patient_explanation: Part of the brain has been pushed out of its usual compartment due to pressure buildup.
clinical_context: A life-threatening emergency requiring immediate treatment to relieve pressure on the brain.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Usually benign tumour of the brain's covering
patient_explanation: There is a growth arising from the membranes covering the brain, which is usually non-cancerous.
clinical_context: The most common primary benign brain tumour; often monitored rather than immediately treated.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Tumour arising from brain support cells
patient_explanation: There is a growth arising from the supportive tissue cells within the brain.
clinical_context: A category of brain tumours ranging from low-grade (slower growing) to high-grade (more aggressive).
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Fluid-filled pocket near the brain surface
patient_explanation: There is a fluid-filled sac between the brain and one of its covering membranes, usually present from birth.
clinical_context: Typically a benign, incidental finding that rarely causes symptoms unless large.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Brain tissue extending into the spinal canal
patient_explanation: Part of the lower brain sits lower than usual, extending slightly into the top of the spinal canal.
clinical_context: Can be an incidental finding or cause symptoms like headache, depending on the degree of descent.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Fluid-filled cavity in the spinal cord
patient_explanation: There is a fluid-filled channel that has formed within the spinal cord.
clinical_context: Can be associated with Chiari malformation, trauma, or spinal cord tumours.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Loss of the brain/spinal cord's protective nerve coating
patient_explanation: Areas of the brain or spinal cord have lost some of the protective coating around nerve fibres.
clinical_context: A key feature of conditions like multiple sclerosis, though it can have other causes too.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Old area of softened brain tissue
patient_explanation: There is an area of the brain where tissue has softened, usually the result of an old injury or stroke.
clinical_context: Represents chronic tissue damage from a prior event such as stroke, trauma, or infection.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Correlate with clinical history; routine follow-up

patient_explanation: The fluid-filled chambers deep within the brain are larger than normal.
clinical_context: Can reflect hydrocephalus (fluid buildup) or, in some cases, brain volume loss.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Shrinkage of the brain's coordination centre
patient_explanation: The part of the brain that helps coordinate movement and balance has reduced in size.
clinical_context: Can occur with ageing or be linked to specific neurological conditions affecting balance and coordination.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Small benign growth on the pituitary gland
patient_explanation: There is a small, usually benign growth on the pituitary gland at the base of the brain.
clinical_context: Very common and often incidental; some produce hormones that may need monitoring or treatment.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

simple_meaning: Bulge in a brain blood vessel wall
patient_explanation: There is a small bulge or ballooning in the wall of one of the blood vessels in the brain.
clinical_context: Unruptured aneurysms are often monitored; risk of rupture depends on size and location.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: There is an abnormal tangle of blood vessels where arteries connect directly to veins, bypassing normal tissue.
clinical_context: Congenital vascular abnormality that carries a risk of bleeding and may need treatment.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Sign of very recent tissue injury
patient_explanation: A pattern on the scan suggests an area of brain tissue has been recently and acutely injured.
clinical_context: A key MRI finding used to identify acute stroke within hours of onset.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Stroke in a border-zone brain area
patient_explanation: A stroke has occurred in an area of the brain that sits at the border between two blood supply territories.
clinical_context: Often related to a period of low blood pressure or blood flow rather than a single blocked vessel.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

patient_explanation: A small area of the deep brain tissue has been damaged by a blocked tiny blood vessel.
clinical_context: Common in people with longstanding high blood pressure or diabetes affecting small brain vessels.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.
follow_up: Vascular risk factor management and neurology follow-up

simple_meaning: Small lump in the thyroid gland
patient_explanation: A small growth has been found in the gland at the front of your neck.
clinical_context: Very common; most thyroid nodules are benign but some need further testing.
action_note: Further evaluation with blood tests or biopsy may be advised.
follow_up: Endocrinology referral; fine needle aspiration if indicated

patient_explanation: The gland at the front of your neck is larger than normal.
clinical_context: Can be diffuse or multinodular; often related to thyroid function or iodine levels.
action_note: Thyroid function blood tests are usually recommended.

simple_meaning: Benign growth on the adrenal gland
patient_explanation: There is a small, usually harmless growth on the gland that sits above your kidney.
clinical_context: Very common incidental finding; almost always benign and non-functioning.
action_note: Usually reassuring; hormone tests may be advised if large.
follow_up: Hormone workup if size or symptoms warrant

patient_explanation: An abnormal growth has been found in the kidney that needs further evaluation.
clinical_context: Can range from benign cysts to renal cell carcinoma; characterization is important.
action_note: This needs prompt urology or oncology review.
follow_up: Urology referral; further imaging or biopsy often needed

patient_explanation: There is a benign, fat-containing growth in the kidney.
clinical_context: Common benign renal tumour; large ones carry a small bleeding risk.
action_note: Usually monitored; larger lesions may need treatment.
follow_up: Surveillance imaging; urology referral if large

simple_meaning: Kidneys joined together at the bottom
patient_explanation: Your two kidneys are fused together at the bottom, forming a U-shape; this is present from birth.
clinical_context: A congenital variant, usually incidental but can predispose to stones or infection.
action_note: Usually no action needed unless symptomatic.

simple_meaning: Multiple fluid-filled cysts in the kidneys
patient_explanation: Both kidneys contain many fluid-filled sacs, which can affect how well they work over time.
clinical_context: Often an inherited condition that can progress to kidney impairment.
action_note: Kidney function monitoring is important.

simple_meaning: Benign growth in the womb muscle
patient_explanation: There is a non-cancerous growth in the muscle wall of the uterus.
clinical_context: Very common benign finding; can vary in size and cause symptoms depending on location.
action_note: Often monitored; treatment depends on symptoms.

patient_explanation: A fluid-filled sac has formed on the ovary; these are usually harmless.
clinical_context: Simple cysts are typically functional and resolve on their own; complex ones need follow-up.
action_note: Simple cysts are usually reassuring; complex ones need follow-up.
follow_up: Repeat ultrasound if simple; gynaecology referral if complex

patient_explanation: The inner lining of the uterus appears thicker than expected.
clinical_context: Significance depends on age, menopausal status, and symptoms.
action_note: Further evaluation may be recommended, especially after menopause.
follow_up: Gynaecology referral; biopsy may be advised

simple_meaning: Womb lining tissue growing into the muscle wall
patient_explanation: Tissue that normally lines the womb has grown into the muscular wall of the uterus.
clinical_context: Common cause of heavy or painful periods; a benign condition.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.

patient_explanation: One of the tubes connecting the ovary to the uterus is blocked and filled with fluid.
clinical_context: Often related to past infection; can affect fertility.
action_note: This should be interpreted with symptoms and doctor advice.
follow_up: Gynaecology referral, especially if fertility is a concern

patient_explanation: The gland below the bladder in men is larger than normal.
clinical_context: Very common with age; can cause urinary symptoms by pressing on the bladder outlet.
action_note: Usually benign; treatment depends on urinary symptoms.

simple_meaning: Abnormal area in the prostate gland
patient_explanation: An area in the prostate gland looks different from the surrounding tissue and needs further checking.
clinical_context: Can range from benign changes to prostate cancer; further work-up guided by risk scoring.
action_note: Further evaluation with blood tests or biopsy is often recommended.
follow_up: Urology referral; PSA testing; possible biopsy

simple_meaning: Abnormal tissue extending into nearby gland
patient_explanation: An abnormal area appears to extend into the glands next to the prostate.
clinical_context: A sign used in staging prostate cancer if present.
action_note: This requires prompt oncology or urology review.

patient_explanation: An abnormal lump or area has been found in the breast tissue.
clinical_context: Can be benign or malignant; further imaging and possibly biopsy guide diagnosis.
action_note: Further imaging or biopsy is often recommended.
follow_up: Breast specialist referral; core biopsy may be advised

patient_explanation: A non-cancerous, firm lump has been found in the breast; these are very common.
clinical_context: Most common benign breast tumour, especially in younger women.
action_note: Usually reassuring; monitoring may be advised.

simple_meaning: Small calcium deposits in the breast
patient_explanation: Tiny calcium spots have been found in the breast tissue on your mammogram.
clinical_context: Pattern and distribution determine whether further work-up is needed.
action_note: Follow-up imaging or biopsy may be advised depending on pattern.
follow_up: Diagnostic mammogram; biopsy if suspicious pattern

patient_explanation: A fluid-filled sac has been found in the breast; these are usually harmless.
clinical_context: Very common, especially in women aged 35-50; simple cysts are benign.
action_note: Simple cysts are almost always benign.

patient_explanation: A lymph node in the armpit area has been noted, which may appear enlarged.
clinical_context: Can be reactive/benign or, in some contexts, related to breast cancer spread.
action_note: Correlate with breast findings and clinical history.

simple_meaning: Infected or inflamed pouches in the colon
patient_explanation: Small pouches in the wall of the colon have become inflamed or infected.
clinical_context: A complication of diverticulosis; severity ranges from mild to complicated with abscess or perforation.
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional; antibiotics may be needed.

patient_explanation: The small pouch attached to the large intestine is inflamed, often requiring urgent treatment.
clinical_context: Common surgical emergency; can progress to rupture if untreated.
action_note: This requires urgent surgical evaluation.
follow_up: Urgent surgical review; appendectomy often needed

patient_explanation: The gland that helps with digestion and blood sugar control is inflamed.
clinical_context: Can be mild or severe; common causes include gallstones and alcohol use.
action_note: This requires prompt medical assessment.
follow_up: Hospital admission often required; treat underlying cause

patient_explanation: A fluid-filled sac has been found in the pancreas; most are benign but some need monitoring.
clinical_context: Includes a range of cystic lesions; some subtypes carry malignant potential.
action_note: Follow-up imaging is often recommended depending on features.

patient_explanation: The tubes that carry bile from the liver appear wider than normal.
clinical_context: Often indicates a downstream blockage; cause needs to be identified.
action_note: Further evaluation is needed to identify the cause.

simple_meaning: Stone in the main bile duct
patient_explanation: A stone has been found in the main tube that carries bile from the liver to the intestine.
clinical_context: Can cause blockage, infection, or jaundice; often needs endoscopic removal.
action_note: This often requires prompt treatment to prevent infection.

patient_explanation: The gallbladder is inflamed, often due to a blocked stone.
clinical_context: Common surgical condition; may need urgent removal of the gallbladder.
synonyms_in_report: gallbladder wall thickening with pericholecystic fluid
action_note: This requires prompt medical/surgical assessment.

patient_explanation: The liver shows widespread scarring, which affects how well it works.
clinical_context: End-stage of chronic liver disease; increases risk of complications.
action_note: Ongoing hepatology follow-up is important.
follow_up: Hepatology referral; surveillance for liver cancer

patient_explanation: An area in the liver shows features suspicious for a cancerous growth.
clinical_context: Most common primary liver cancer; often develops in cirrhotic livers.
synonyms_in_report: arterial enhancing liver lesion with washout
action_note: This requires urgent oncology and hepatology review.

patient_explanation: There are areas in the liver that appear to be cancer that has spread from elsewhere in the body.
clinical_context: Common site of spread for many cancers; guides staging and treatment planning.
synonyms_in_report: hypodense hepatic lesions consistent with metastases
common_causes: Spread from colon, breast, lung, or other primary cancer
action_note: This requires urgent oncology review.

simple_meaning: Abnormal growth in the colon or rectum
patient_explanation: An abnormal growth has been found in the large intestine that needs further evaluation.
clinical_context: Can be benign polyp or malignant tumour; colonoscopy and biopsy needed for diagnosis.
action_note: This requires prompt gastroenterology/oncology evaluation.

simple_meaning: Small growth on the colon lining
patient_explanation: A small growth has been found on the inner lining of the colon.
clinical_context: Most are benign but some types can progress to cancer over time.
action_note: Removal during colonoscopy is often recommended.

patient_explanation: There are signs of ongoing inflammation in part of your digestive tract, consistent with a chronic bowel condition.
clinical_context: A type of inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the GI tract.
synonyms_in_report: bowel wall thickening consistent with Crohn disease
action_note: Ongoing gastroenterology management is recommended.

simple_meaning: Chronic inflammation of the colon lining
patient_explanation: The lining of your large intestine shows ongoing inflammation.
clinical_context: A type of inflammatory bowel disease limited to the colon and rectum.
synonyms_in_report: colonic mucosal inflammation consistent with UC
action_note: Ongoing gastroenterology management is recommended.

patient_explanation: Part of the abdominal contents has pushed through a weak spot in the groin muscle wall.
clinical_context: Common finding; can sometimes become trapped (incarcerated), needing urgent repair.
action_note: Surgical repair may be advised, especially if symptomatic.

simple_meaning: Bulge through a previous surgical scar
patient_explanation: Part of the abdominal contents has pushed through a weak area at a prior surgery site.
clinical_context: Common complication of abdominal surgery; can enlarge over time.
synonyms_in_report: incisional hernia at prior surgical site
action_note: Surgical repair may be advised depending on size and symptoms.

patient_explanation: There is a break in the lining of the stomach, causing a sore area.
clinical_context: Can be caused by infection or medication use; usually treatable.
action_note: This should be discussed with a doctor for treatment.

simple_meaning: Stomach pushing up into the chest
patient_explanation: Part of the stomach has moved up through the diaphragm into the chest cavity.
clinical_context: Common finding, especially with age; can contribute to acid reflux symptoms.
action_note: Often manageable with lifestyle changes or medication.

simple_meaning: Thickened wall of the small intestine
patient_explanation: The wall of the small intestine appears thicker than normal.
clinical_context: Can be due to inflammation, infection, or, less commonly, tumour.
action_note: Further evaluation is needed to determine the cause.

simple_meaning: Reduced blood flow to the intestines
patient_explanation: The blood supply to part of the intestines appears reduced, which can be serious.
clinical_context: A medical emergency that can lead to bowel damage if untreated.
action_note: This is a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment.

simple_meaning: Area of dead tissue in the spleen from lost blood supply
patient_explanation: Part of the spleen has been damaged due to a temporary loss of blood supply.
clinical_context: Can occur with blood clots or clotting disorders; usually managed conservatively.
action_note: The underlying cause should be investigated.

simple_meaning: Enlarged lymph nodes behind the abdominal cavity
patient_explanation: Lymph nodes located toward the back of your abdomen appear larger than normal.
clinical_context: Can reflect infection, inflammation, or malignancy; often needs further work-up.
action_note: The cause needs to be determined with further tests.
follow_up: Oncology referral; biopsy may be needed

simple_meaning: Small growth on the gallbladder wall
patient_explanation: A small growth has been found on the inner wall of the gallbladder.
clinical_context: Most are benign cholesterol polyps; size guides whether monitoring or removal is needed.
action_note: Usually monitored; removal advised if large or growing.
follow_up: Surveillance ultrasound; surgical review if large

simple_meaning: Bulge through the abdominal wall muscles
patient_explanation: Part of the abdominal contents has pushed through a weak area of the abdominal wall.
clinical_context: Can occur at various sites including umbilical, epigastric, or spigelian locations.
action_note: Surgical repair may be advised depending on symptoms.

simple_meaning: One isolated small spot in the lung
patient_explanation: A single small round spot has been found in your lung.
clinical_context: Very common finding; management depends on size, shape, and growth over time.
action_note: Follow-up imaging is often recommended based on size.
follow_up: Follow-up CT per Fleischner Society guidelines

simple_meaning: Larger abnormal growth in the lung
patient_explanation: A larger abnormal growth has been found in the lung that needs further evaluation.
clinical_context: Larger than a nodule (over 3cm); carries higher likelihood of malignancy and needs prompt work-up.
action_note: This requires prompt respiratory/oncology review.
follow_up: Urgent respiratory referral; biopsy often needed

simple_meaning: Abnormal growth in the central chest space
patient_explanation: An abnormal growth has been found in the central area of the chest, between the lungs.
clinical_context: Can arise from many structures; location within the mediastinum helps narrow the cause.
action_note: This requires prompt further evaluation.

patient_explanation: There is a growth arising from a gland located in the upper chest behind the breastbone.
clinical_context: Usually slow-growing; can sometimes be associated with autoimmune conditions.
synonyms_in_report: anterior mediastinal mass consistent with thymoma
action_note: Discuss this finding with a healthcare professional.

simple_meaning: Thickened wall of the food pipe
patient_explanation: The wall of the tube that carries food from your mouth to the stomach appears thicker than normal.
clinical_context: Can be due to inflammation, infection, or tumour; further evaluation often needed.
action_note: Further evaluation with endoscopy is often recommended.

simple_meaning: Abdominal contents pushed into the chest through the diaphragm
patient_explanation: Part of the abdominal organs has moved up into the chest through a gap in the diaphragm.
clinical_context: Can be congenital or acquired, often following trauma or surgery.
action_note: Surgical review is usually recommended.

patient_explanation: One or more of your rib bones is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Common after trauma; can be associated with underlying lung or organ injury.
action_note: Pain management and monitoring for complications is advised.

patient_explanation: The bone connecting your shoulder to your breastbone is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Common injury, especially after falls onto the shoulder.
action_note: Orthopaedic review advised, especially if displaced.

patient_explanation: The upper part of your thigh bone near the hip joint is broken.
clinical_context: Common in older adults, especially after a fall; usually requires surgery.
action_note: This requires urgent orthopaedic treatment.

simple_meaning: Broken bone in the wrist area
patient_explanation: A bone near your wrist is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Common after a fall onto an outstretched hand.
action_note: Orthopaedic review is advised for proper healing.

patient_explanation: One of the bones forming your ankle joint is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Common injury from twisting or falls; stability of the ankle joint guides treatment.
action_note: Orthopaedic review is advised, especially if unstable.
follow_up: Orthopaedic assessment; casting or surgery if unstable

patient_explanation: One or more bones of your pelvis are cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Can range from minor to life-threatening depending on associated bleeding and organ injury.
action_note: This requires urgent trauma team assessment.

patient_explanation: There is a crack or break in one of the bones of your skull.
clinical_context: Can be associated with underlying brain injury; needs careful assessment.
action_note: This requires urgent neurosurgical assessment.

patient_explanation: One of the bones in your neck spine is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: A serious injury that can affect the spinal cord; requires careful stabilization.
action_note: This requires urgent spine specialist assessment.

patient_explanation: Something is pressing on the spinal cord, which can affect nerve function.
clinical_context: A medical emergency that can cause permanent nerve damage if not treated promptly.
synonyms_in_report: severe canal stenosis with cord signal change
action_note: This requires emergency neurosurgical assessment.

simple_meaning: Cancer spread to the spine bones
patient_explanation: There are areas in your spine bones that appear to be cancer that has spread from elsewhere.
clinical_context: Common site of cancer spread; can weaken bone and risk fracture or nerve compression.
synonyms_in_report: metastatic disease involving the vertebral bodies
common_causes: Breast, prostate, lung, or other primary cancer spread
action_note: This requires urgent oncology review.
follow_up: Urgent oncology referral; radiation therapy may be needed

patient_explanation: There are signs of a tuberculosis infection affecting the bones of your spine.
clinical_context: A form of skeletal tuberculosis that can cause bone destruction and deformity.
synonyms_in_report: vertebral body destruction with paraspinal abscess
action_note: This requires prompt infectious disease and spine specialist treatment.

patient_explanation: One of the cushioning discs in your spine appears to be infected.
clinical_context: A serious infection that requires prompt antibiotic treatment.
action_note: This requires urgent treatment.

simple_meaning: Narrowed neck artery supplying the brain
patient_explanation: One of the main arteries in your neck that supplies blood to the brain has become narrowed.
clinical_context: A risk factor for stroke; severity determines whether intervention is needed.
action_note: Vascular surgery or neurology review is often recommended.

simple_meaning: Tear in the wall of the main artery
patient_explanation: There is a tear in the inner layer of your main blood vessel, which is a serious emergency.
clinical_context: A life-threatening emergency requiring immediate treatment.
action_note: This is a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment.

patient_explanation: The arteries supplying blood to your legs have become narrowed, reducing blood flow.
clinical_context: Common in smokers and those with diabetes; can cause leg pain with walking.
action_note: Discuss risk factor management with your doctor.

patient_explanation: Veins, usually in the legs, have become enlarged and twisted due to poor valve function.
clinical_context: Common and usually benign; can cause discomfort or skin changes if severe.
action_note: Treatment is usually elective and symptom-based.

simple_meaning: Contained blood collection outside a vessel wall
patient_explanation: A pocket of blood has formed outside the wall of a blood vessel, often after a procedure or injury.
clinical_context: Can occur after catheter procedures or trauma; may need closure to prevent rupture.
action_note: This should be evaluated promptly by a vascular specialist.

patient_explanation: The air-filled spaces around your nose and eyes appear inflamed, often due to infection.
clinical_context: Very common; usually managed with medical treatment.
action_note: Usually managed with medical treatment.
follow_up: ENT referral if chronic or recurrent

patient_explanation: The wall dividing the two sides of your nose is bent to one side.
clinical_context: Very common; can contribute to nasal breathing difficulty.
action_note: Treatment is only needed if causing symptoms.

simple_meaning: Infection of the bone behind the ear
patient_explanation: The bony area behind your ear is infected, often following an ear infection.
clinical_context: Can be a serious complication of ear infection requiring prompt treatment.
action_note: This requires prompt medical treatment.

simple_meaning: Abnormal area on the voice box
patient_explanation: An abnormal area has been found on one of your vocal cords.
clinical_context: Can be benign (nodules, polyps) or, less commonly, malignant.
action_note: Further evaluation with an ENT specialist is recommended.

simple_meaning: Stone blocking a saliva gland duct
patient_explanation: A small stone is blocking the tube that carries saliva from a gland into your mouth.
clinical_context: Can cause swelling and pain, especially with eating.
action_note: Usually managed conservatively; removal may be needed.

simple_meaning: Congenital fluid-filled sac in the neck midline
patient_explanation: There is a fluid-filled sac in the middle of your neck that has been present since birth.
clinical_context: A common congenital neck mass, usually benign.
action_note: Surgical removal may be advised, especially if symptomatic.

patient_explanation: One of the bones surrounding your eye is cracked or broken.
clinical_context: Often follows facial trauma; can affect eye movement if severe.
action_note: Ophthalmology/ENT review is advised, especially if vision affected.

simple_meaning: Separation of the light-sensing layer at the back of the eye
patient_explanation: The layer of the eye that senses light has separated from its normal position.
clinical_context: A serious eye emergency that can cause vision loss if untreated.
action_note: This requires urgent ophthalmology treatment.

simple_meaning: Swollen or thickened nerve to the eye
patient_explanation: The nerve connecting your eye to the brain appears swollen or thickened.
clinical_context: Can relate to inflammation, increased pressure, or, less commonly, tumour.
action_note: This should be evaluated by an ophthalmologist or neurologist.

patient_explanation: There is a pocket of infection at the root of one of your teeth.
clinical_context: Common dental infection; needs prompt dental treatment.
action_note: This requires prompt dental treatment.

patient_explanation: The joint that connects your jaw to your skull shows changes consistent with joint dysfunction.
clinical_context: Common cause of jaw pain and clicking; usually managed conservatively.
action_note: Usually managed with conservative treatment.

simple_meaning: Pocket of infection under the skin
patient_explanation: There is a collection of pus under your skin, indicating an infection.
clinical_context: Common soft tissue infection; may need drainage.
action_note: Drainage and antibiotics may be needed.

simple_meaning: Infection of the skin and soft tissue
patient_explanation: The skin and tissue underneath appear inflamed due to an infection spreading through the area.
clinical_context: Common bacterial skin infection; usually treated with antibiotics.
synonyms_in_report: soft tissue edema and stranding consistent with cellulitis
action_note: This should be treated promptly with antibiotics.
follow_up: Medical treatment; monitor for abscess formation

simple_meaning: Rapidly spreading, severe soft tissue infection
patient_explanation: There are signs of a severe, fast-spreading infection affecting the deep tissue layers.
clinical_context: A surgical emergency with high mortality if not treated immediately.
synonyms_in_report: fascial gas and fluid concerning for necrotizing fasciitis
action_note: This is a surgical emergency requiring immediate treatment.

simple_meaning: Growth in the muscle or fat tissue
patient_explanation: An abnormal growth has been found in the soft tissue, such as muscle or fat.
clinical_context: Most are benign (lipomas), but characterization is needed to exclude sarcoma.
action_note: Further imaging or biopsy may be advised.
follow_up: Orthopaedic oncology referral if suspicious features

patient_explanation: A soft, benign lump made of fatty tissue has been found.
clinical_context: Very common and almost always benign.
action_note: Usually reassuring; removal only if symptomatic.
follow_up: No routine follow-up needed unless symptomatic

simple_meaning: Cancer of muscle, fat, or connective tissue
patient_explanation: There is a growth that shows features suspicious for a cancer arising from soft tissue.
clinical_context: A rarer type of cancer arising from connective tissue; requires urgent specialist review.
synonyms_in_report: heterogeneous mass with necrosis suspicious for sarcoma
action_note: This requires urgent oncology review.

simple_meaning: Collection of blood outside blood vessels
patient_explanation: A collection of blood has formed in the tissue, usually after injury.
clinical_context: Usually resolves on its own; large ones may need drainage.
action_note: Usually monitored; drainage advised if large or symptomatic.
follow_up: Monitor resolution; surgical drainage if large

simple_meaning: Collection of clear fluid, usually after surgery
patient_explanation: A pocket of clear fluid has formed, often at the site of a recent surgery.
clinical_context: Common post-surgical finding; usually resolves on its own.
action_note: Usually resolves on its own; drainage if symptomatic.
follow_up: Monitor; drainage if large or infected

patient_explanation: There is enlarged glandular tissue in the male breast area.
clinical_context: Common and usually benign, often related to hormonal changes.
action_note: Usually benign; further evaluation if rapidly growing.

patient_explanation: An abnormal growth has been found in the testicle that needs further evaluation.
clinical_context: Can be benign or malignant; ultrasound features help guide next steps.
action_note: This requires prompt urology evaluation.

patient_explanation: A benign, fluid-filled sac has been found near the testicle.
clinical_context: Very common and benign finding.
action_note: Usually reassuring; no treatment needed unless symptomatic.

patient_explanation: Fluid has collected in the sac surrounding the testicle.
clinical_context: Common and usually benign, though large ones may need drainage.
common_causes: Fluid accumulation in the tunica vaginalis
action_note: Usually reassuring; treatment only if symptomatic.
follow_up: Urology referral if large or symptomatic

simple_meaning: Twisted testicle cutting off blood supply
patient_explanation: The testicle has twisted, which can cut off its blood supply and is a medical emergency.
clinical_context: A surgical emergency; prompt treatment is needed to save the testicle.
synonyms_in_report: absent testicular blood flow consistent with torsion
action_note: This is a surgical emergency requiring immediate treatment.

patient_explanation: An abnormal growth has been found on the inner lining of the bladder.
clinical_context: Requires further evaluation, usually with cystoscopy, to determine the cause.
action_note: This requires prompt urology evaluation.

patient_explanation: The wall of your bladder appears thicker than normal.
clinical_context: Can be due to chronic infection, outlet obstruction, or, less commonly, tumour.
action_note: Further evaluation may be recommended.

patient_explanation: The tube that carries urine out of the body has become narrowed.
clinical_context: Can cause difficulty urinating; often needs urology treatment.
action_note: Urology evaluation is recommended.

patient_explanation: A pregnancy is developing outside the uterus, most often in a fallopian tube.
clinical_context: A medical emergency due to risk of internal bleeding if the tube ruptures.
action_note: This is a medical emergency requiring immediate treatment.

simple_meaning: Placenta covering the birth canal opening
patient_explanation: The placenta is positioned low in the uterus, covering or near the opening of the cervix.
clinical_context: Can cause bleeding in pregnancy; affects delivery planning.
action_note: This requires close obstetric monitoring.
follow_up: Obstetric follow-up; repeat imaging as pregnancy progresses

simple_meaning: Baby smaller than expected for gestational age
patient_explanation: The baby appears smaller than expected for this stage of pregnancy.
clinical_context: Requires monitoring to check on baby's wellbeing and growth trend.
action_note: This requires close obstetric monitoring.

patient_explanation: There is less amniotic fluid around the baby than expected.
clinical_context: Can be associated with various causes; requires further evaluation and monitoring.
action_note: This requires close obstetric monitoring.

patient_explanation: There is more amniotic fluid around the baby than expected.
clinical_context: Can be associated with maternal diabetes or fetal conditions; needs further evaluation.
action_note: Further evaluation may be recommended.

simple_meaning: Increased fluid at the back of baby's neck
patient_explanation: A measurement at the back of the baby's neck is higher than the expected range for this stage.
clinical_context: A screening marker used with blood tests to assess chromosomal risk.
action_note: Further genetic counselling and testing may be recommended.

simple_meaning: Structural difference in the baby's heart
patient_explanation: The scan shows a structural difference in the developing baby's heart.
clinical_context: Requires detailed fetal cardiac assessment and specialist counselling.
action_note: This requires prompt specialist evaluation.
follow_up: Maternal-fetal medicine and paediatric cardiology referral

simple_meaning: Abnormal tissue growth instead of a normal pregnancy
patient_explanation: The tissue in the uterus shows features of an abnormal type of pregnancy tissue growth rather than a developing baby.
clinical_context: Requires prompt evaluation and treatment; monitored closely afterward.
action_note: This requires prompt gynaecology/oncology treatment.

simple_meaning: Abnormal hip joint development in infants
